scope: Public primary sources. No claim of global obscurity, exhaustive novelty search, or successful upstream reproduction. Product concepts are proposals, not paper results.

works.title: NL2Plan: Robust LLM-Driven Planning from Minimal Text Descriptions
works.venue: arXiv; repository now calls the work Assistive PDDL Modeling
works.status: adaptation candidate; original stack integration risk
works.mechanism: Translate natural-language domain/problem descriptions into PDDL, then use a classical planner.
works.proposed_product: A fixed-domain scheduling or resource-allocation assistant with editable constraints, a solver check, and explanations of infeasibility.
works.minimum_spike: Use typed JSON for one small domain and a constraint solver; do not reproduce the entire PDDL pipeline by default.
works.baseline: Human-readable greedy assignment and, if budget allows, LLM-only output validated by the same checker.
caveats: Solver guarantees only apply to the model actually encoded.
The JSON/solver version is inspired by the paper, not a reproduction.
Original repo recommends Docker/Linux/WSL and notes macOS untested. LLM access still required.

works.title: Practical Rateless Set Reconciliation
works.status: best non-LLM systems candidate; Go integration needed
works.mechanism: Exchange coded symbols to discover the symmetric difference between two sets without first knowing its size.
works.proposed_product: Offline inventory synchronization across two simulated branches over a throttled connection.
works.minimum_spike: Run the author example. Synchronize immutable versioned record hashes, then fetch missing payloads and verify full-set equality.
works.baseline: Full snapshot transfer plus a sorted-hash-list difference baseline; add Merkle/log-based sync before broad efficiency claims.
metrics: total on-wire bytes including hashes and payloads
caveats: Not a conflict-resolution algorithm, database, or secure transport.
Mutations/deletions need a versioning and tombstone policy.
A tiny app can have more overhead than a straightforward change log; measure crossover.
works.local_execution: not run: container could not resolve github.com for git clone

works.title: Collaborative Text Editing with Eg-walker: Better, Faster, Smaller
works.license_observed: TypeScript reference package.json declares BSD-2-Clause; this is not a blanket license for all repository content. Retain/check the chosen component notices.
works.status: usable TypeScript reference declared BSD-2-Clause; check integration and component notices first
works.mechanism: Event-graph-based collaborative text editing that targets memory/loading and divergent-branch merging weaknesses.
works.proposed_product: Offline-first incident notes: two users edit disconnected copies, reconnect, and see a converged text history.
works.minimum_spike: Use the TypeScript reference to test concurrent inserts/deletes on tiny traces; optimized benchmarks use a different implementation.
works.baseline: Established collaborative-text library plus a clearly labeled last-write-wins failure example.
caveats: Reference-code speed is not evidence for optimized-paper performance.
Convergent text can still have semantic contradictions; show them for review.
Do not run the entire paper benchmark suite during the hackathon.

works.title: Hallucination Detection on a Budget: Efficient Bayesian Estimation of Semantic Entropy
works.status: laptop-friendly estimator experiments using precomputed outputs; live integration is extra work
works.mechanism: Bayesian estimation of uncertainty over answer meanings, with adaptive allocation of additional answer samples.
works.proposed_product: An evidence-triage interface that flags unstable answers and routes them to source review rather than asserting correctness.
works.minimum_spike: Reproduce a small precomputed estimator experiment, then use a tiny labeled domain dataset for live evaluation.
works.baseline: Fixed sample-count semantic entropy at matched generation budget; single-answer/no-filter baseline.
caveats: Consistent wrong answers can have low entropy.
Existing laptop reproduction uses precomputed responses; fresh generation can require GPU/API resources.
Inspect any pickle provenance before loading; never unpickle untrusted files.
Prior fitting, semantic clustering, and test data must remain separated.

works.title: Evidential Semantic Entropy for LLM Uncertainty Quantification
works.license_observed: No license verified in reviewed repository root.
works.status: newer specialist lead; not the default next-day code dependency
works.mechanism: Represent uncertainty from both relationships among observed answer meanings and possible but unobserved meanings.
works.proposed_product: A research comparison for uncertainty-aware evidence triage, not a claim to determine truth.
works.minimum_spike: Read the method and check a tiny worked example; copy code only after verifying reuse permission.
works.baseline: Standard semantic entropy and the Bayesian estimator on the same labeled outputs.
caveats: Research code and model-generation requirements can consume the event.
No verified license means code reuse remains unresolved.
Method is not a universal hallucination detector.

works.title: Conformal Risk Control; newer lead: Conformal Risk Control for Non-Monotonic Losses
works.license_observed: MIT for original repository; no extension implementation verified.
works.status: original method usable if labeled calibration data already exists; new extension research-only
works.mechanism: Choose a prediction-set parameter using calibration data to control expected bounded monotone loss under exchangeability; newer work relaxes monotonicity via algorithm-stability conditions.
works.proposed_product: A service-request router that returns a small candidate set or asks a discriminating question when ambiguity remains.
works.minimum_spike: Keep training, calibration and test examples separate; calibrate the original monotone set-valued formulation.
works.baseline: Uncalibrated top-1 and fixed-threshold prediction sets at comparable coverage or set size.
caveats: This is not a per-person safety probability.
Exchangeability, calibration size and loss assumptions matter.
Do not imply the old code implements the 2026 extension.
This field is established, not claimed to be globally unknown.
